- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is falling.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been trending sharply upward for 5+ days, model often fails to revert; forecast should show gradual decline.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price increases (last 7-10 days); add 2-5% buffer to end of forecast if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1-2 days ahead of actual trend.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; sentiment should be averaged over 3-5 days for model calibration.
